name: Benjamin Brighton
title: One new project every day
tagline: Small projects on the questions I keep coming back to: why AI stalls at the pilot stage, fintech, markets, retail, carbon and more. Practice, not polish.
how: Every project starts with a question of mine, drawn from my research, my work and the business I help run. I pick the themes and the questions, then turn each idea into a working app, with the assistance of various AI tools. Every app runs in your browser, works offline and uses synthetic data.
about: I'm a final-year Business and Management with Legal Studies student at the University of Sussex. One question runs through most of what I do: why does AI so often stall at the pilot stage, in companies and in people's everyday lives?

The ideas come from my own experience: interviewing senior executives about AI transformation as a research associate, building AI tools and CRM reports in a global sales team, and growing a confectionery business I co-founded from an online shop to ten outlets. Each project takes one of those questions, turns it into a small tool you can try and writes up what it shows.

Some are about AI adoption, how people and AI make decisions together, fintech and AI regulation. Others come from the things I do outside my degree: consulting, trading challenges, retail forecasting, carbon, sport and languages.

They are practice pieces, not finished products: quick, focused and sometimes rough at the edges. The numbers come from invented, synthetic data, so treat them as ways of thinking about a problem rather than forecasts.
footer: One new project every day. Synthetic data, nothing confidential, everything runs in your browser.
projectNote: The app above runs entirely in your browser on synthetic data. The full source code, including any companion version and its tests, is on GitHub.
